This pull request introduces significant improvements to the admin settings for authentication, particularly around enabling SSO-only login, and enhances user safety with a new warning modal. It also updates the navigation logic for signup visibility, refines default branding, and improves i18n support for new features.

**Authentication Settings & SSO-Only Mode**

* Added a dedicated toggle for "Only SSO Login" (`disableCredentialsLogin`) in the admin settings, with logic to ensure `allowSignin` is true when SSO-only is enabled. The UI disables this toggle unless an SSO provider is active and provides user feedback if not. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3a95e7031b2395b7cbae89a205d4ac9696465971d2ca2cfdc93f6f71f7a44975R67-R106) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3a95e7031b2395b7cbae89a205d4ac9696465971d2ca2cfdc93f6f71f7a44975R199-R243)

body:
### Motivation
- Make the project easier to run, deploy and understand by adding concise docs and an `.env` template.
- Improve reliability of Notion requests by centralizing HTTP retry behavior and logging of status/payload.
- Make the Telegram flows friendlier and safer by setting sensible defaults and returning clear user-facing error messages.
- Respect existing architecture and Notion property names while adding role-aware behavior for editors/viewers.

### Description
- Refresh `README.md` with `What it does`, `Env vars` (with example), `Run locally`, `Receive webhook locally`, `Set Telegram webhook` and `Deploy to Cloud Run` sections and provide example commands like `ngrok`, `cloudflared`, `curl` and `gcloud`.
- Add `.env.example` containing `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `NOTION_TOKEN`, `NOTION_ORDERS_DB_ID`, `NOTION_MODELS_DB_ID`, `ALLOWED_EDITORS`, and `TIMEZONE`.
- Add `safe_request` helper in `app/notion.py` and delegate `NotionClient._request` to it to perform retries only on `429`/`5xx` responses while logging `status` and a short payload excerpt.
- Improve error handling and UX in `app/handlers/orders.py`: wrap Notion calls with `try/except` to log exceptions and return user-friendly messages like "Notion error, try again.", set default `qty=1` when type is chosen, show a clear read-only message for viewers on `/orders_close`, clear close buttons after successful close via `edit_reply_markup`, and ensure state is cleared on errors.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.
- Local manual run instructions were added to `README.md` for running the server and exposing a webhook via `ngrok` or `cloudflared` for manual testing.

author: milos-lk
body:
OnTrackUnsubscribed doesn't come in band with media data, some media data might still be buffered on SFU side when egress proceeds with reacting on this signal by stopping its read loop and draining all internally buffered data. This might result in missing to read last buffered samples on the SFU side. 
The goal of this change is to try to read all data from SFU - even after `OnTrackUnsubscribed` is received by not stopping the read loop and allowing up to grace period to read remaining media. Instead of stopping, keep record of the received unsubscribed signal and keep reading until either EOF or an unexpected error is received or grace period expires - at which point data will be drained as usual.

Fixes AINFRA-1869

See paaHJt-9BZ-p2 and and https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce-ios/pull/16588

### Description
This PR is the result of exploring ideas on extracting context for localization strings based on the codebase.
For this, I've been using a gem that I've _vibe-built_, https://github.com/iangmaia/txcontext. The idea is to add (or enhance) context to all strings and then have a process where they're continuously added in an automated way.
Then, once we have better detailed context, we will have better quality automated (or human) translations.

**Note**: we can tweak a few configuration parameters such as the size of the code context for each string to fine tune what yields better context quality.

**The idea of this PR is just to review the context that has been added so far, the quality, and to validate if the idea makes sense in general.**

## Why I'm doing:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Parquet files with empty `null_counts` in ColumnIndex cause SIGSEGV crash during page index filtering. 

  The `null_counts` field is optional in the Parquet specification, and some writers(like SnowFlake export to Iceberg) don't populate it. 
  When StarRocks reads such files with  predicates that trigger page index filtering, it crashes due to out-of-bounds vector access.                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ## What I'm doing:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Add bounds check before accessing `column_index.null_counts[i]` in `scalar_column_reader.cpp`. The fix changes:                                                                                                                                    
  ```cpp                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
bool has_null = column_index.null_counts[i] > 0;   
```                                                                                                                                                                                                
  to:  
```cpp
bool has_null = i >= column_index.null_counts.size() || column_index.null_counts[i] > 0; 
 ```

body: ## Summary This PR makes the Favorite Messages button always visible when the favorites feature is enabled, displaying an empty state message when no favorites exist instead of hiding the button completely. ## Motivation Currently, the button is hidden when users have no favorites, which makes the feature hard to discover. New users may not even know the favorites feature exists until they accidentally star a message. ## Changes ### Component Updates - **FavoriteButton.tsx**: - Added `CommandEmpty` import - Removed empty check that hid the button (`if (!favorites.length) return null;`) - Implemented conditional rendering to show empty state or favorites list ### Empty State UI When no favorites exist, users now see: - **Title**: "No Saved Prompts Yet" - **Description**: "Start by sending a prompt and star it or star a prompt from previous chats" ### Translations - Added `chat.favorites.empty.title` and `chat.favorites.empty.description` keys to all 20 translation files - Translations provided for: en-US, es, fr-FR, de-DE, it, nl, ja, zh-CN, zh-TW, ko, el-GR, he-IL, bn, hi, gu, kn, ml, mr, ta, te ### Tests - Updated translation mock with new keys - Modified test to expect button with empty state instead of null - Added new test to verify empty state message display ## Before & After **Before**: Button completely hidden when no favorites exist **After**: Button visible with helpful empty state message ## Testing - [x] Button appears when favorites feature is enabled and no favorites exist - [x] Empty state message displays correctly - [x] Button works normally when favorites are present - [x] Feature flag still respected (button hidden when `features.favorites = false`) - [x] All tests updated and passing ## Impact This change improves feature discoverability without affecting existing functionality. Users with existing favorites will see no difference, while new users will immediately see the favorites feature is available. --- ## Summary by cubic Always show the Favorite Messages button when the favorites feature is enabled, and display a friendly empty state when no favorites exist. This improves discoverability for new users. - **New Features** - Button is always visible when favorites are enabled; hidden only when the feature flag is off. - Added an empty state in the popover using CommandEmpty with localized title and description. - Conditional rendering switches between the empty state and the favorites list. - Added empty-state translation keys in 20 locales and updated tests to cover the new behavior. Written for commit f29b48c9e2ea469453262d0ed79fc8cf021d87a6. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
## Summary

When the backend returns a 401 Unauthorized or AUTH_REQUIRED error, the CLI now automatically triggers the login flow to re-authenticate instead of just showing an error message.

Additionally, on startup the session is validated with the server to catch cases where the token was revoked server-side even though the local credentials appear valid.

## Problem

Users were seeing 'Authentication required' (401) errors when sending messages even though they appeared to be logged in locally. This happened because the local credentials check only verified local token expiration, not server-side token validity.

## Changes

1. **Runtime error handling** (`event_loop.rs`):
   - Added detection for authentication errors (401, unauthorized, auth_required, etc.) in `StreamEvent::Error` handler
   - When auth error is detected, show a system message and trigger the login flow modal

2. **Startup validation** (`app_runner.rs`):
   - After loading local auth credentials, validate them with the server
   - If server rejects the token (401/403), show login screen immediately instead of proceeding with invalid credentials

3. **Session validation API** (`manager.rs`):
   - Added `validate_session()` method to `ProviderManager` that makes an authenticated API call to check token validity
   - Returns `Ok(false)` if server returns 401/403, `Ok(true)` if successful, `Err` for network errors

## Testing

The changes maintain backward compatibility and gracefully handle:
- Valid sessions: continue normally
- Server-revoked sessions: show login screen
- Network errors during validation: continue with local auth status (don't block user)
- Runtime auth errors: trigger login flow

Fixes the issue where users appear logged in but get AUTH_REQUIRED errors when sending messages.

body:
Overview
- Introduces a complete PHP-based CMS designed for shared hosting (cPanel), with a WordPress-like installer, MySQL or file-based JSON storage, and a full admin/frontend workflow. The stack includes a lightweight MVC-like structure, secure sessions, CSRF protection, and a responsive UI built with Tailwind.

What this PR delivers
- End-to-end, production-ready architecture:
  - PHP backend with a minimal framework (routing, controllers, models, views) and a simple PSR-4 autoloader.
  - MySQL or file-based JSON storage options, with real relational schema when using MySQL and a safe flat-file fallback with JSON for file-based mode.
  - Admin panel for managing tools and pages, plus a dashboard with basic analytics.
  - Automatic tool page generation when a tool is created; tools render as card-based blocks on the main dashboard and load a real tool interface.
  - A page/content builder for unlimited pages with per-page SEO settings and slug-based URLs.
  - A robust installer with browser-based steps for site data, database selection (MySQL or file JSON), admin account creation, and automatic config generation. Installer locks after successful setup via a storage install.lock file.
  - Custom error pages (404, 403) and a dedicated maintenance mode framework scaffold.
  - A security-first approach: CSRF protection, password hashing, prepared queries, basic rate limiting scaffolding, and input validation.
  - File-based caching and a simple error-logging path baked into the config system.
  - Public frontend for the tools dashboard and tool detail pages; admin routes for managing content, users, tools, and pages.
  - Admin analytics (counts of users/tools/pages) and an ON/OFF website switch concept.

Key components touched
- Installer (install/):
  - Step-by-step wizard with options for MySQL or file JSON storage, admin account creation, and auto-configuration of app/database config files.
  - Locks after installation via storage/install.lock to prevent re-install.
- Core framework (app/):
  - Controllers: AuthController, DashboardController, ToolController, PageController, etc.
  - Models: User, Tool, Page with dual storage backends (MySQL or file-based JSON).
  - Core: Config, Database, Request, Router, Session, View, and helper utilities.
- Data layer (app/Core, app/Models):
  - Database class with prepared statements for MySQL; JSON-based persistence wrappers for file mode.
  - Models expose convenient helpers: Tool::enabledTools(), Tool::findBySlug(), Page::findBySlug(), User::current()/isAdmin(), etc.
- Admin UI (Views):
  - Admin dashboard with analytics, Tools management, Pages management; API-like routes wired for admin tasks.
  - Tool cards on the frontend dashboard with “Go Now” to launch tool interface in-app.
- Frontend views (app/Views/):
  - layouts/main.php as a single layout with header/footer, and individual views for login, register, dashboard, tools, pages, errors, and content.
- Installer assets (install/):
  - Full installation flow, MySQL/file driver selection, admin creation, and final completion screen with a redirect to the site.
- Security and routing:
  - CSRF token helpers (csrf_token, verify_csrf_token) and e() helper for escaping.
  - Public routes and admin routes structured in config/routes.php.

Database schemas (MySQL)
- Users, Tools, Pages, Settings, Activity logs, Login history with foreign keys and basic indexing defined in install/schema.sql.
- Prepared statements used for all user/tool/page queries to prevent SQL injection.

How to deploy on shared hosting
- Upload project, point web root to public/ (public_html or equivalent).
- Ensure PHP 7.4+ and MySQL availability; set writable directories: storage/, config/.
- Access installer at /install/ and follow the wizard:
  - Step 1: Choose storage (MySQL or file JSON), provide DB credentials if MySQL, site name, and base URL.
  - Step 2: Create admin account (email/password).
  - Step 3: Installer completes, creates install.lock, and the site is ready.
- After installation, visit frontend at / and admin at /admin with the created admin account.

Files and deliverables
- Full project architecture with folder structure and namespace layout.
- Database schemas for MySQL (in install/schema.sql) and corresponding model-level file-based equivalents.
- Installer workflow and lock mechanism to prevent reinstallation.
- Auto page creation flow for new tools and admin pages, plus content/PAGE builder.
- Custom error pages (404, 403) and routing rules for shared hosting (.htaccess provided).
- Admin workflow including tool and page management and activity counts for dashboards.
- Step-by-step hosting installation guide included in README.md.

Notes
- This implementation targets production-readiness for shared hosting environments with PHP-based backends, MySQL or file JSON storage, and a WordPress-like installer.
- The codebase is designed to be extended: you can introduce richer WYSIWYG editors, more granular roles, richer analytics, and advanced security controls as needed.
- Firebase client-side optional integration is cursory in this release and can be added in a future iteration if required.

### Prerequisites

- [x] I have added steps to test this contribution in the description below

### Description

This PR fixes an issue where PNG images converted to WebP with resize parameters matching the original dimensions resulted in files ~20x larger than expected.

#### The Problem

When using the ImageSharp URL generator with both `format=webp` and `width`/`height` parameters, the generated URL placed resize parameters **before** the format parameter:

```
/media/image.png?width=1708&height=1037&format=webp  → 1.49 MB (Lossless)
```

ImageSharp.Web processes commands in query string order. When the resize is a no-op (dimensions match the original), the configured Lossy WebP encoder was not being applied correctly, resulting in Lossless encoding and much larger files.

#### The Fix

Move the `format` parameter to be added **before** `width`/`height` in the query string:

```
/media/image.png?format=webp&width=1708&height=1037  → 70 KB (Lossy)
```

This ensures ImageSharp.Web applies the configured encoder settings correctly regardless of whether an actual resize occurs.

#### Changes

- `ImageSharpImageUrlGenerator.cs` (both v3 and v2 packages): Reorder format parameter placement
- Added regression tests to verify correct parameter ordering

#### How to Test

1. Upload a PNG image to the media library
2. Request it with format conversion and resize matching original dimensions:
   - Before fix: `?width={original}&height={original}&format=webp` → Large file
   - After fix: `?format=webp&width={original}&height={original}` → Small file
3. Run unit tests: `dotnet test --filter "ImageSharpImageUrlGeneratorTests"`

This can also been seen on the hero image on the umbraco.com homepage:
Before: https://umbraco.com/media/hvjlhtfw/home-full-screen-4.png?width=1708&height=1037&format=webp (1.5MB)
After: https://umbraco.com/media/hvjlhtfw/home-full-screen-4.png?format=webp&width=1708&height=1037 (73.5KB)

## Why I'm doing:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Parquet files with empty `null_counts` in ColumnIndex cause SIGSEGV crash during page index filtering. 

  The `null_counts` field is optional in the Parquet specification, and some writers(like SnowFlake export to Iceberg) don't populate it. 
  When StarRocks reads such files with  predicates that trigger page index filtering, it crashes due to out-of-bounds vector access.                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ## What I'm doing:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Add bounds check before accessing `column_index.null_counts[i]` in `scalar_column_reader.cpp`. The fix changes:                                                                                                                                    
  ```cpp                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
bool has_null = column_index.null_counts[i] > 0;   
```                                                                                                                                                                                                
  to:  
```cpp
bool has_null = i >= column_index.null_counts.size() || column_index.null_counts[i] > 0; 
 ```                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Fixes #66403
